newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares closed at a record high despite profit taking that undermined midday all-time highs above 3,838 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
Sentiment was good given Wall Street's record run and a strong U.S. dollar, dealers said.

"I think we can take the 3,900 SMI level by the end of this month", one trader noted. "We may see some profit taking, but at the same time some people may find they missed the latest upswing and start buying."
SMI ended higher by 0.22 percent or 8.5 points at 3,822.2, beating the prior mark of 3,818.1 set on October 8). The intra-day high was 3,838.7 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 5.37 points, or 0.22 percent, to 2,446.25 points.
Volumes were above those on Monday, one dealer said.
The firming U.S. dollar helped financials. ABB and Alusuisse were up 1.67 and 0.95 percent, respectively.
Nestle, which led the actives list, added 11 francs to 1,413.

Roche profited from better-than-expected sales figures for the first nine months of 1996 and switches from Ciba and Sandoz. The certificates ended up 50 francs to 9,705, falling back from highs above the strong resistance level of 9,755 francs.
SMH, which has been under pressure from a sell note by Standard & Poor's Marketscope following a review of the Smart Car project, finished unchanged at 820.
Among financials, CS Holding made up for recent lows, adding nearly one percent to 127.50 francs.
UBS bearer shares, which had seen lively interest in the past few days, fell three francs to 1,256.
Sulzer gained 1.86 percent to 767 ahead of a press conference on Thursday about a restructuring at textile machinery unit Sulzer Rueti.
